# Reference Case A — Agent access to secrets

**Codokey Reference Cases v1.0.0 · validator `tools/codokey-check.mjs`**

> Repository access is not the same thing as credential access. Whether an agent can read a secret depends on where the secret lives and on the boundary that enforces exclusion — not on whether the agent was "given the repo".

## Scenario

A task agent is asked to fix a bug in a small service. Its workspace is a checkout of the repository. The checkout contains a local .env file, a placeholder key file, and an INI file with a hardcoded token — the kinds of files that commonly sit beside code. The agent can run commands (tests, scripts).

## Assumptions

- All credentials in the fixture are fake strings.
- The agent configuration is declared in JSON; the validator reads the declaration, it does not observe a running agent.
- "enforcement" records the strongest boundary covering the deny rules: "tool" (agent tool-level rules only), "os-sandbox" (OS/sandbox isolation covering subprocesses), or "not-in-workspace" (secrets absent from the workspace).

## Synthetic inputs

- repo/ — synthetic repository with .env, config/deploy_key.pem, config/settings.ini, and a harmless .env.example
- agent-config.governed.json — deny rules cover every secret-bearing file; os-sandbox enforcement; no production variables
- agent-config.ungoverned.json — only .env denied; tool-level enforcement with command execution; a PROD_ variable in the agent environment

All values are synthetic. No real credentials, repositories, or systems are used.

## Protocol layers

02 Key Exposure, 03 Agent Authority

## Control expectations

- Every secret-bearing file is outside the agent's readable set (CK-KE-03).
- The exclusion holds for subprocesses, not only the agent's file tool (CK-KE-03).
- No production credential is in the agent environment (CK-KE-06, forbidden zone FZ-1).

## Observable pass/fail conditions

| Check | Condition |
|---|---|
| A1 | PASS if every file identified as secret-bearing matches a deny rule. |
| A2 | PASS if enforcement is os-sandbox or not-in-workspace; tool-level rules alone FAIL when the agent can run commands. |
| A3 | PASS if no environment variable name contains PROD. |

## Evidence requirements (real-world equivalent)

Agent configuration export (deny rules, sandbox setting), list of secret-bearing paths from a scan, a recorded denied read attempt, and the agent environment variable names (names only).

## Reproduce

```sh
node tools/codokey-check.mjs secrets-access --repo cases/a-secrets-access/repo --agent cases/a-secrets-access/agent-config.governed.json   # expect PASS
node tools/codokey-check.mjs secrets-access --repo cases/a-secrets-access/repo --agent cases/a-secrets-access/agent-config.ungoverned.json   # expect FAIL (A1, A2, A3)
```

## Expected outcome

governed → PASS. ungoverned → FAIL on A1 (deploy_key.pem and settings.ini readable), A2 (tool-level only), A3 (production variable present).

## Limitations

- Secret detection uses filename patterns and a simple assignment pattern; it will miss secrets in other forms and is not a substitute for a secret scanner.
- The PROD naming heuristic is illustrative; real environments need an explicit classification of variables.
- A PASS does not prove the agent product honors its declared configuration.
